passages.text: Thus the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now the Israelites went out to meet the Philistines in battle and camped at Ebenezer, while the Philistines camped at Aphek.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of the LORD.
All Israel knew Samuel was a prophet.
Samuel spoke God’s word to all Israel.
The Israelites prepared for battle against the Philistines.
The Israelites camped at Ebenezer.
The Philistines camped at Aphek.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל לְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּצֵ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵל֩ לִקְרַ֨את פְּלִשְׁתִּ֜ים לַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ עַל־ הָאֶ֣בֶן הָעֵ֔זֶר וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים חָנ֥וּ בַאֲפֵֽק׃

passages.text: The Philistines arrayed themselves against Israel, and as the battle spread, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who struck down about four thousand men on the battlefield.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines prepared for battle against Israel.
The Philistines faced Israel in war.
The battle began and spread across the field.
Israel was defeated by the Philistines.
The Philistines killed about four thousand Israelite men on the battlefield.
passages.original: וַיַּעַרְכ֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֜ים לִקְרַ֣את יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַתִּטֹּשׁ֙ הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַיִּנָּ֥גֶף יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לִפְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּכּ֤וּ בַמַּֽעֲרָכָה֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה כְּאַרְבַּ֥עַת אֲלָפִ֖ים אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: When the troops returned to the camp, the elders of Israel asked, “Why has the LORD brought defeat on us before the Philistines today? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, so that it may go with us to save us from the hand of our enemies.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel returned to their camp.
The elders of Israel spoke to the people.
The elders asked, “Why did the LORD let us be defeated today by the Philistines?”
The elders said, “Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD here from Shiloh.”
They said, “Then the ark will come among us.”
They said, “It will save us from the power of our enemies.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א הָעָם֮ אֶל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֒ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָ֣מָּה נְגָפָ֧נוּ יְהוָ֛ה הַיּ֖וֹם לִפְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים נִקְחָ֧ה אֵלֵ֣ינוּ מִשִּׁלֹ֗ה אֶת־ אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְיָבֹ֣א בְקִרְבֵּ֔נוּ וְיֹשִׁעֵ֖נוּ מִכַּ֥ף אֹיְבֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: So the people sent men to Shiloh, and they brought back the ark of the covenant of the LORD of Hosts, who sits enthroned between the cherubim. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel sent men to Shiloh.
The men brought back the ark of the covenant of the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD of Hosts sits enthroned between the cherubim.
Hophni and Phinehas were the two sons of Eli.
Hophni and Phinehas were with the ark of the covenant of God.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח הָעָם֙ שִׁלֹ֔ה וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֗ם אֵ֣ת אֲר֧וֹן בְּרִית־ יְהוָ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַכְּרֻבִ֑ים וְשָׁ֞ם שְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־ עֵלִ֗י עִם־ אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים חָפְנִ֖י וּפִֽינְחָֽס׃

passages.text: When the ark of the covenant of the LORD entered the camp, all the Israelites raised such a great shout that it shook the ground.
passages.sermon:
The ark of the covenant of the LORD entered the camp.
All the Israelites shouted loudly.
Their shout was very great.
The ground shook.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כְּב֨וֹא אֲר֤וֹן בְּרִית־ יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיָּרִ֥עוּ כָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תְּרוּעָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַתֵּהֹ֖ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: On hearing the noise of the shout, the Philistines asked, “What is this loud shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?” And when they realized that the ark of the LORD had entered the camp, the Philistines were afraid. “The gods have entered their camp!” they said. “Woe to us, for nothing like this has happened before.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines heard the sound of the great shout.
They asked, “What is this loud shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?”
The Philistines learned that the ark of the LORD had entered the camp.
The Philistines became afraid.
They said, “God has come into the camp.”
They said, “Woe to us!”
They said, “Nothing like this has happened before.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמְע֤וּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ אֶת־ ק֣וֹל הַתְּרוּעָ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֶ֠ה ק֣וֹל הַתְּרוּעָ֧ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֛ה הַזֹּ֖את בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה הָעִבְרִ֑ים וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֚י אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה בָּ֖א אֶל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃ וַיִּֽרְאוּ֙ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים כִּ֣י אָמְר֔וּ בָּ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיֹּאמְרוּ֙ א֣וֹי לָ֔נוּ כִּ֣י לֹ֥א הָיְתָ֛ה כָּזֹ֖את אֶתְמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֹֽׁם׃

passages.text: Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines spoke.
They were afraid.
They said, “Woe to us!”
They asked, “Who will save us from these mighty gods?”
They called the God of Israel mighty.
They remembered what God did in Egypt.
They said, “These are the gods who struck Egypt.”
They said, “They sent many plagues in the wilderness.”
passages.original: א֣וֹי לָ֔נוּ מִ֣י יַצִּילֵ֔נוּ מִיַּ֛ד הָאֱלֹהִ֥ים הָאַדִּירִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה אֵ֧לֶּה הֵ֣ם הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים הַמַּכִּ֧ים אֶת־ מִצְרַ֛יִם בְּכָל־ מַכָּ֖ה בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: Take courage and be men, O Philistines! Otherwise, you will serve the Hebrews just as they served you. Now be men and fight!”
passages.sermon:
The Philistines were a powerful enemy of Israel.
A Philistine leader spoke to his people.
He said, “Be strong.
Be brave.
Be men, Philistines.
If you are not strong, you will become slaves to the Hebrews.
The Hebrews were your slaves before.
Now you must be men.
You must fight.”
passages.original: הִֽתְחַזְּק֞וּ וִֽהְי֤וּ לַֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים פֶּ֚ן תַּעַבְד֣וּ לָעִבְרִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָבְד֖וּ לָכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶ֥ם לַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים וְנִלְחַמְתֶּֽם׃

passages.text: So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tent. The slaughter was very great—thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines fought against Israel.
The Philistines defeated Israel.
Each Israelite man ran away to his own tent.
The defeat was very great.
Thirty thousand Israelite foot soldiers died.
passages.original: וַיִּלָּחֲמ֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיִּנָּ֤גֶף יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיָּנֻ֙סוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְאֹהָלָ֔יו וַתְּהִ֥י הַמַּכָּ֖ה גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וַיִּפֹּל֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף רַגְלִֽי׃

passages.text: The ark of God was captured, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines captured the ark of God.
Eli had two sons.
Their names were Hophni and Phinehas.
Hophni died.
Phinehas died.
passages.original: וַאֲר֥וֹן אֱלֹהִ֖ים נִלְקָ֑ח וּשְׁנֵ֤י בְנֵֽי־ עֵלִי֙ מֵ֔תוּ חָפְנִ֖י וּפִֽינְחָֽס׃

passages.text: That same day a Benjamite ran from the battle line all the way to Shiloh, with his clothes torn and dirt on his head.
passages.sermon:
A man from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battle line.
He ran on the same day as the battle.
He came to the city of Shiloh.
His clothes were torn.
There was dirt on his head.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤רָץ אִישׁ־ בִּנְיָמִן֙ מֵהַמַּ֣עֲרָכָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֥א שִׁלֹ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וּמַדָּ֣יו קְרֻעִ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־ רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: When he arrived, there was Eli, sitting on his chair beside the road and watching, because his heart trembled for the ark of God. When the man entered the city to give a report, the whole city cried out.
passages.sermon:
Eli was an old priest.
Eli was ninety-eight years old.
Eli could not see.
Eli sat on his chair beside the road.
Eli watched and waited.
Eli’s heart trembled for the ark of God.
A man arrived from the battle.
The man came to give a report in the city.
The whole city cried out when the man entered.
passages.original: וַיָּב֗וֹא וְהִנֵּ֣ה עֵ֠לִי יֹשֵׁ֨ב עַֽל־ הַכִּסֵּ֜א יַךְ דֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ מְצַפֶּ֔ה כִּֽי־ הָיָ֤ה לִבּוֹ֙ חָרֵ֔ד עַ֖ל אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְהָאִ֗ישׁ בָּ֚א לְהַגִּ֣יד בָּעִ֔יר וַתִּזְעַ֖ק כָּל־ הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Eli heard the outcry and asked, “Why this commotion?” So the man hurried over and reported to Eli.
passages.sermon:
Eli was an old priest.
Eli was ninety-eight years old.
Eli could not see.
Eli heard the sound of people crying out.
Eli asked, “What is the meaning of this noise?”
A man came quickly to Eli.
The man told Eli what had happened.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע עֵלִי֙ אֶת־ ק֣וֹל הַצְּעָקָ֔ה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מֶ֛ה ק֥וֹל הֶהָמ֖וֹן הַזֶּ֑ה וְהָאִ֣ישׁ מִהַ֔ר וַיָּבֹ֖א וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לְעֵלִֽי׃

passages.text: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his gaze was fixed because he could not see.
passages.sermon: Eli was ninety-eight years old.\r\nEli could not see.\r\nEli’s eyes were fixed.
passages.original: וְעֵלִ֕י בֶּן־ תִּשְׁעִ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנֶ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה וְעֵינָ֣יו קָ֔מָה וְלֹ֥א יָכ֖וֹל לִרְאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: “I have just come from the battle,” the man said to Eli. “I fled from there today.” “What happened, my son?” Eli asked.
passages.sermon:
Eli was ninety-eight years old.
Eli could not see.
A man came to Eli.
The man said, “I have just come from the battle.”
The man said, “I fled from the battle today.”
Eli asked, “What happened, my son?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הָאִ֜ישׁ אֶל־ עֵלִ֗י אָֽנֹכִי֙ הַבָּ֣א מִן־ הַמַּעֲרָכָ֔ה וַאֲנִ֕י מִן־ הַמַּעֲרָכָ֖ה נַ֣סְתִּי הַיּ֑וֹם וַיֹּ֛אמֶר מֶֽה־ הָיָ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּנִֽי׃

passages.text: The messenger answered, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are both dead, and the ark of God has been captured.”
passages.sermon:
A messenger spoke to Eli.
Eli was an old priest who could not see.
The messenger said, “Israel has run away from the Philistines.
The Philistines are Israel’s enemies.
There was a great defeat among the people of Israel.
Many Israelites died.
Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead.
The ark of God has been captured.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן הַֽמְבַשֵּׂ֜ר וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָ֤ס יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לִפְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְגַ֛ם מַגֵּפָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה הָיְתָ֣ה בָעָ֑ם וְגַם־ שְׁנֵ֨י בָנֶ֜יךָ מֵ֗תוּ חָפְנִי֙ וּפִ֣ינְחָ֔ס וַאֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים נִלְקָֽחָה׃פ

passages.text: As soon as the ark of God was mentioned, Eli fell backward from his chair by the city gate, and being old and heavy, he broke his neck and died. And Eli had judged Israel forty years.
passages.sermon:
Eli was an old and heavy man.
Eli had judged Israel for forty years.
Someone mentioned the ark of God.
Eli sat on a chair by the city gate.
When he heard about the ark, Eli fell backward from his chair.
He fell by the gate.
Eli broke his neck.
Eli died.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י כְּהַזְכִּיר֣וֹ׀ אֶת־ אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים וַיִּפֹּ֣ל מֵֽעַל־ הַ֠כִּסֵּא אֲחֹ֨רַנִּ֜ית בְּעַ֣ד׀ יַ֣ד הַשַּׁ֗עַר וַתִּשָּׁבֵ֤ר מַפְרַקְתּוֹ֙ וַיָּמֹ֔ת כִּֽי־ זָקֵ֥ן הָאִ֖ישׁ וְכָבֵ֑ד וְה֛וּא שָׁפַ֥ט אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: Now Eli’s daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and about to give birth. When she heard the news of the capture of God’s ark and the deaths of her father-in-law and her husband, she collapsed and gave birth, for her labor pains overtook her.
passages.sermon:
Eli had a daughter-in-law.
She was the wife of Phinehas.
She was pregnant.
She was about to give birth.
She heard news.
The ark of God had been captured.
Her father-in-law had died.
Her husband had died.
She collapsed.
She gave birth.
Her labor pains overtook her.
passages.original: וְכַלָּת֣וֹ אֵֽשֶׁת־ פִּינְחָס֮ הָרָ֣ה לָלַת֒ וַתִּשְׁמַ֣ע אֶת־ הַשְּׁמֻעָ֔ה אֶל־ הִלָּקַח֙ אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּמֵ֥ת חָמִ֖יהָ וְאִישָׁ֑הּ וַתִּכְרַ֣ע וַתֵּ֔לֶד כִּֽי־ נֶהֶפְכ֥וּ עָלֶ֖יהָ צִרֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: As she was dying, the women attending to her said, “Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son!” But she did not respond or pay any heed.
passages.sermon:
Eli’s daughter-in-law was dying.
She was the wife of Phinehas.
She had just given birth to a son.
Several women stood by her side.
These women spoke to her.
They said, “Do not be afraid.”
They said, “You have given birth to a son.”
She did not answer them.
She did not pay attention to their words.
passages.original: וּכְעֵ֣ת מוּתָ֗הּ וַתְּדַבֵּ֙רְנָה֙ הַנִּצָּב֣וֹת עָלֶ֔יהָ אַל־ תִּֽירְאִ֖י כִּ֣י בֵ֣ן יָלָ֑דְתְּ וְלֹ֥א עָנְתָ֖ה וְלֹא־ שָׁ֥תָה לִבָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: And she named the boy Ichabod, saying, “The glory has departed from Israel,” because the ark of God had been captured and her father-in-law and her husband had been killed.
passages.sermon:
Phinehas’s wife gave birth to a son.
She named the boy Ichabod.
She said, “The glory has departed from Israel.”
She said this because the Philistines captured the ark of God.
She also said this because her father-in-law and her husband died.
passages.original: וַתִּקְרָ֣א לַנַּ֗עַר אִֽי־ כָבוֹד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר גָּלָ֥ה כָב֖וֹד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֶל־ הִלָּקַח֙ אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאֶל־ חָמִ֖יהָ וְאִישָֽׁהּ׃

passages.text: “The glory has departed from Israel,” she said, “for the ark of God has been captured.”
passages.sermon:
A woman spoke.
She said, “The glory has departed from Israel.”
She explained the reason.
She said, “The ark of God has been captured.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר גָּלָ֥ה כָב֖וֹד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֥י נִלְקַ֖ח אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃פ
